help.title: From action to delivery, follow the real creation flow
help.subtitle: Pick a task to view the full flow, step-by-step actions, result handling, and FAQs.

help.flowDescription: Review the stages first, then move into the detailed steps.
help.stepsDescription: Complete the steps in order. Each step includes checklist items.
help.faqDescription: Handle issues based on the real status of the current feature.

start.label: Quick start
start.title: Start creating from one idea
start.summary: For first-time use, start with the creative Agent. It understands goals, reference assets, and delivery format, then routes work to image, video, canvas, or short-drama capabilities.
outcomes: Know which entry to start from
Understand smart planning vs manual models

flow.title: Describe the goal
flow.detail: Explain what to make, who it is for, and where it will be used

flow.title: Add references
flow.detail: Upload people, products, style images, or existing assets

flow.title: Confirm the plan
flow.detail: Keep smart planning on, or choose Skills and models

flow.title: Review results
flow.detail: Preview media, download it, or reuse it in the next round

steps.title: Write a complete goal
steps.description: Do not only write a style word. At least add subject, use case, frame or shot requirements, and the final content you want.
checklist: Subject: person, product, scene, or story
Use case: e-commerce, social, short drama, pitch, or personal work
Constraints: size, duration, count, text, brand colors, and details that must stay
steps.tip: If you are unsure about parameters, keep smart planning on so the Agent first gives a verifiable selection summary.

steps.title: Add references when consistency matters
steps.description: Use the attachment entry to upload images or reuse existing assets. Faces, product looks, logos, and established styles should be provided before sending.
checklist: People consistency: clear frontal face or character sheet
Product consistency: multi-angle product or white-background shots
Style consistency: choose one to three closest reference images

steps.title: Choose how to execute
steps.description: Smart planning matches executable models and parameters by default. Only turn it off and pick one or more models when you already know the model differences.
checklist: Skills are execution capabilities and do not inject a fixed prompt into the input box
Manual model selection turns smart planning off
Clearing manual models restores smart planning

steps.title: Handle generated results
steps.description: Click images or videos to preview them. The asset actions support download and reuse, so you can continue with revisions, extended shots, or matching content.
checklist: Zoom in first to check people, text, edges, and motion continuity
Download results you are happy with
For follow-ups, reference the asset and describe the next change

faqs.question: I do not know whether to choose image, video, or canvas. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Describe the final use case in the creative Agent. Keep smart planning on so the system can infer the delivery type and summarize the choice.

faqs.question: Can I keep editing after generation?
faqs.answer: Yes. Preview the result, then use the reference-asset action under the result to continue the conversation. Switch to a specialized workbench when you need precise parameters.

agent.label: Creative Agent
agent.title: Use Agent from brief to delivery
agent.summary: Best for one-line requests, multi-asset packages, and continuous work across image, video, canvas, and short drama. Conversations and results are saved in server sessions.

flow.title: Enter the request
flow.detail: Describe goal, audience, use case, and deliverables

flow.title: Choose capabilities
flow.detail: Add Skills, reference assets, or manual models as needed

flow.title: Agent planning
flow.detail: Review direction, models, parameters, and product rationale

flow.title: Run tasks
flow.detail: Generate inside the chat and keep task status visible

flow.title: Iterate
flow.detail: Reference results, add constraints, or edit the original message

steps.title: Shape an executable request
steps.description: Use natural language to describe the final delivery. Complex work can be listed, but do not split it into model parameters yourself.
checklist: Goal: for example a product launch asset set
Delivery: for example one hero visual, three detail images, and one short video
Consistency: people, products, and colors that must be reused
Acceptance criteria: what counts as done

steps.title: Add Skills, references, and models
steps.description: Skills sit on the left of the input and become removable cards when selected. The bulb controls smart planning; the model button supports multi-select executable models.
checklist: Only choose a Skill when the task needs that capability
Keep smart planning on by default
Select at most six models for manual comparison
Confirm reference assets appear in the input before sending

steps.title: Read the Agent selection summary
steps.description: The Agent first explains the creative direction and why it chose the current models and parameters. If the direction is wrong, add constraints early instead of waiting for the full wrong batch.
checklist: Check whether subject and use case were understood
Check delivery count and format
Check whether references were used
Check whether model and aspect ratio fit the task

steps.title: Manage messages and sessions
steps.description: User messages support copy and edit; re-editing continues with the new request. History is used to open, rename, select, and delete server sessions.
checklist: Copy: reuse a full request
Edit: fix the original request and run again
New chat: start an unrelated project
History: restore previous context and results

steps.title: Preview, download, and reference media
steps.description: Click media to open a large preview. Download sits under the asset; reference brings the current result back into the input for the next change.
checklist: Preview before deciding to download
When referencing, say what to keep and what to change
Move to the image or video workbench for specialized parameters

faqs.question: Will a Skill automatically rewrite my input?
faqs.answer: No. Selected Skills are submitted as execution capabilities and shown as cards above the input; your original text stays unchanged.

faqs.question: Why does smart planning turn off after I pick models?
faqs.answer: Manual models mean you explicitly set the execution scope, so automatic matching turns off. Clear the model selection to restore smart planning.

image.label: Image workbench
image.title: Generate, refine, and reuse images
image.summary: The image workbench is for single or batch image tasks that need clear control over aspect ratio, count, quality, and reference images.

flow.title: Describe the frame
flow.detail: Subject, environment, composition, lighting, and use case

flow.title: Provide references
flow.detail: People, products, style, or a previous result

flow.title: Confirm parameters
flow.detail: Model, aspect ratio, quality, and generation count

flow.title: Review generation
flow.detail: Check Agent decisions and task progress

flow.title: Reuse results
flow.detail: Preview, download, reference, or keep refining

steps.title: Choose text-to-image or reference-image flow
steps.description: Describe the frame directly when there is no fixed subject. Add reference images first when people, products, or composition must stay consistent.
checklist: People references should be clear and unobstructed
Product references should keep real proportions and key structure
Style references should not conflict with subject references

steps.title: Let the Agent plan first
steps.description: After you enter a request, the Agent decides whether it is a normal single image or a batch task, then matches models and parameters.
checklist: Check whether the recommended aspect ratio fits the placement
Check whether the count is enough for comparison
Check whether text, logos, or reserved blank space are needed

steps.title: Adjust generation parameters as needed
steps.description: Settings show the current model, size, quality, and count. On mobile the parameter panel scrolls vertically, so no horizontal dragging is needed.
checklist: Social square posts often use 1:1
Covers and banners prefer landscape
People posters and vertical content prefer portrait
Higher batch counts usually cost more points

steps.title: Inspect and handle results
steps.description: After generation, click an image to preview and check subject consistency, text, hands, edges, and materials.
checklist: Happy with it: download
Direction is right but details are weak: reference the result and continue refining
Direction is wrong: fix the goal or references in the request

faqs.question: Why was my reference image not used?
faqs.answer: Confirm the reference already appears in the input area, and explicitly say what people, product, or composition to keep. If you only upload without stating the purpose, the Agent may treat it as a style reference.

faqs.question: Where is image history?
faqs.answer: The workbench history area shows this user's server generation records. Opening a historical result lets you preview, download, or use it as the next reference.

video.label: Video workbench
video.title: Create text-to-video and image-to-video
video.summary: The video workbench controls first-frame references, camera motion, duration, aspect ratio, and audio options for single-shot clips and image animation.

flow.title: Choose a starting point
flow.detail: Create from text only, or add an image as the first frame

flow.title: Describe motion
flow.detail: Subject action, camera, pacing, and what must not change

flow.title: Confirm settings
flow.detail: Model, duration, aspect ratio, quality, and audio

flow.title: Wait for the task
flow.detail: Watch submit, generation, and normalization progress

flow.title: Review the clip
flow.detail: Play the preview, download, or reference for follow-up work

steps.title: Decide whether to use a first-frame image
steps.description: Use image-to-video when a specific person, product, or composition must stay. Use text-to-video when the camera can be freer.
checklist: First-frame ratio should be close to the target video ratio
Avoid blurry or heavily cropped images
For image-to-video, clearly say which elements must stay unchanged

steps.title: Describe action and camera separately
steps.description: First say what the subject does, then how the camera moves, and finally pacing, lighting, and forbidden changes.
checklist: Subject action: turn, walk, expression, or product motion
Camera: push-in, pull-out, orbit, follow, or locked-off
Pacing: slow, natural, fast, or staged
Stability: no face morphing, deformation, drifting text, or extra objects

steps.title: Confirm duration, aspect ratio, and audio
steps.description: The settings panel shows current video parameters. Audio is collapsed by default; expand it only when sound is needed.
checklist: Choose mobile-friendly ratios for vertical content
Longer durations need clearer shot changes
Keep audio off when sound is not needed
Manual models only show currently enabled executable channels

steps.title: Handle task status
steps.description: Video generation usually takes longer than images. Pausing the chat stops the current Agent flow; when a task fails, adjust the input from the error and retry.
checklist: Do not repeatedly submit the same request
On failure, first check model, references, and duration hints
Play the full video before downloading a success

faqs.question: Why is the model list empty?
faqs.answer: The frontend only shows currently executable video models. If none are available, the page clearly says no enabled video capability is configured.

faqs.question: What if the generated duration does not match settings?
faqs.answer: The server normalizes results to the target duration. If normalization is impossible, the task fails explicitly instead of registering media with the wrong duration as success.

canvas.label: My Canvas
canvas.title: Connect a full creation flow with nodes
canvas.summary: Canvas is for putting text, images, video, audio, and panoramas into one project, then organizing references, generation, and follow-up edits through connections.

flow.title: Create a project
flow.detail: Start a new project or continue an existing one from the canvas list

flow.title: Add nodes
flow.detail: Double-click empty space or choose a type from the connection menu

flow.title: Organize references
flow.detail: Connect text, image, video, and audio nodes

flow.title: Generate and edit
flow.detail: Use Agent or node tools to run tasks

flow.title: Review delivery
flow.detail: Preview, download, copy prompts, or keep connecting

steps.title: Create nodes and organize space
steps.description: After entering a project, double-click empty canvas space to create a node, or pick the next node type from an existing node's connection entry.
checklist: Text nodes: store prompts, scripts, and notes
Image nodes: import or generate images
Video and audio nodes: organize media results
Panorama nodes: generate 2:1 environment panoramas

steps.title: Use connections for reference relationships
steps.description: Connect reference nodes to the target node. The target input can use @ to mention connected assets, and numbering is refreshed from current connections before sending.
checklist: Connect first, then generate from the target node
Before deleting a connection, confirm later nodes no longer need that reference
Arrange complex projects from upstream references to downstream results

steps.title: Use Canvas Agent
steps.description: The top-right Agent panel supports current project context, Skills, smart planning, and multi-model selection, and can create or update nodes from a request.
checklist: Say whether to add or modify existing nodes
Select current nodes or assets when references are needed
Check the Agent plan and target node type
Pausing the chat stops the current execution flow

steps.title: Generate and inspect panorama nodes
steps.description: Select a panorama node, enter an environment description, and the system generates a 2:1 equirectangular result. Successful results support drag-based immersive viewing inside the node.
checklist: Recommended size is 2048×1024
Describe the horizon and scene center clearly
Avoid normal banners, fisheye circles, and obvious seams
After generation, drag the view to check left-right continuity and top/ground integrity

steps.title: Use node result tools
steps.description: Select or hover a media node to preview, download, copy prompts, edit locally, upscale, or continue generation through connections.
checklist: Download important results first
Copy prompts to review parameters later
Keep the original node before generating again so versions can be compared

faqs.question: Why is there no asset in the @ list?
faqs.answer: Only images or text already connected to the current target node appear in the mention list. Create the connection first, then open the input and choose it.

faqs.question: Why can't a panorama be viewed immersively?
faqs.answer: Panorama assets need a near 2:1 ratio and must be registered as panorama nodes. Ordinary image nodes do not switch to the panorama viewer even if they are very wide.

drama.label: Short drama projects
drama.title: Move from synopsis to a deliverable short drama
drama.summary: The drama workspace organizes script structure, characters and scenes, storyboard review, shot generation, voiceover, subtitles, and final export by project.
outcomes: Save versions and export subtitles or finals

flow.title: Create the project
flow.detail: Fill in project goals, audience, and story direction

flow.title: Extract structure
flow.detail: Agent organizes script, characters, scenes, and episodes

flow.title: Review content
flow.detail: Confirm shots, dialogue, subtitles, and visual plans

flow.title: Batch production
flow.detail: Generate storyboards, shot videos, and voiceover

flow.title: Compose and export
flow.detail: Adjust subtitle timing and output the final or draft package

steps.title: Create a project with a clear production goal
steps.description: Create a project from the drama list and first clarify genre, audience, platform, duration, and episode count. Existing story text can be given directly to the drama Agent.
checklist: Target duration per episode
Main characters and relationships
Conflict and ending direction
Platform aspect ratio and content limits

steps.title: Extract structure with Agent
steps.description: The Agent turns input into an editable project structure rather than only returning chat text. After generation, check characters, scenes, episodes, and shots one by one.
checklist: Keep character names and looks unique
Avoid duplicate scene meanings
Each episode needs a clear beginning, middle, and end
Shot dialogue and subtitles must match the story

steps.title: Review content before batch generation
steps.description: In content review, correct shot order, framing, action, dialogue, and visual prompts. Only enter production after the full visual plan is confirmed.
checklist: Can the shot finish within the target duration
Are character and scene references correct
Is dialogue suitable for voiceover
Do subtitles need to differ from dialogue
steps.tip: Save a version before batch generation so later rework can restore quickly.

steps.title: Generate storyboards, shots, and voiceover
steps.description: You can generate shot by shot or batch unfinished items. The project queue submits in order to avoid creating too many concurrent tasks.
checklist: Finish storyboard images before generating video shots
Retry failed shots instead of creating the same task again
Generate voiceover only for shots with dialogue
You can cancel the current task during generation

steps.title: Handle subtitles, versions, and export
steps.description: Check each line on the subtitle timeline and export SRT if needed. Compose the episode only after all shots and required voiceovers are ready. Projects also support version history and Jianying draft export.
checklist: Check whether subtitles exceed shot duration
Save current changes before restoring a version
Play the full final once after composition
Export a Jianying ZIP draft when further editing is needed

faqs.question: Why can't I generate the final directly?
faqs.answer: Final composition depends on reviewed shot videos, required voiceovers, and subtitle timing. The page points out unfinished production stages so missing assets are not composed.

faqs.question: Will regenerating overwrite the old version?
faqs.answer: A project snapshot is saved before critical regenerations, and you can also save versions manually. Open version history and restore a specific version when you need to roll back.

assets.label: My Assets
assets.title: Organize and reuse creative assets
assets.summary: The asset library stores this user's text, images, video, and audio. Search by type, title, tags, and source, then reuse them in canvas and creation flows.
outcomes: Reference assets in other creation flows

flow.title: Collect assets
flow.detail: Upload files, add URLs, or save generation results

flow.title: Add metadata
flow.detail: Fill in title, source, and searchable tags

flow.title: Search and preview
flow.detail: Filter by type, keyword, and tags

flow.title: Reuse and deliver
flow.detail: Copy text, download media, or insert into canvas

steps.title: Add the correct asset type
steps.description: The new-asset dialog supports text, image, video, and audio. Choose the type first, then fill content or upload a file.
checklist: Write titles that stay searchable later
Record whether the source is upload, generation, or project
Use stable tags such as person, product, project, or style
Do not save secrets or private information as text assets

steps.title: Preview, edit, and download
steps.description: Asset cards provide preview and management actions. Text can be copied, media can be downloaded, and title, tags, and source can still be edited.
checklist: Open preview before downloading
Editing only changes the asset record and does not auto-update historical projects that already referenced it
Before deleting, confirm no project still depends on the asset

steps.title: Reference assets while creating
steps.description: Agent results can be referenced directly; Canvas asset pickers load the current user's assets when first opened.
checklist: Confirm the asset card appears in the input after referencing
Say whether the asset is for subject, style, or first frame
Use clear tags in large projects to keep search efficient

faqs.question: Why are assets not shown right after opening?
faqs.answer: Assets load from the server for the current user. The first open shows a compact loading state; if loading fails, use the retry action on the page.

faqs.question: Will deleting an asset break projects?
faqs.answer: The server checks references from creative sessions, Canvas, drama, and generation records. Media still in use is not deleted directly, so projects do not end up with missing files.

prompts.label: Prompts
prompts.title: Find, save, and reuse prompts
prompts.summary: The public prompt library is for structure and inspiration; My Prompts is for personal templates. Both support copy, and personal prompts are added through a modal.
outcomes: Know the difference between prompts and Skills

flow.title: Search for inspiration
flow.detail: Filter public content by title, category, and tags

flow.title: Open details
flow.detail: Confirm structure and suitable scenarios

flow.title: Copy and rewrite
flow.detail: Replace subject, use case, style, and constraints

flow.title: Save a template
flow.detail: Record a personal version in the My Prompts modal

steps.title: Narrow the range with categories and tags
steps.description: Public prompts can be many. Choose a category first, then use tags and keywords. Mobile uses dropdown filters instead of horizontal scrolling.
checklist: First choose a category by image, video, or other use
Continue with industry, style, and subject tags
Open details before copying the full content

steps.title: Rewrite examples into your own request
steps.description: Public prompts are structural references, not ready-to-submit final text. Replace placeholders and add real subjects, references, and delivery limits.
checklist: Replace brand, person, product, and scene
Remove style words that do not fit the current project
Add aspect ratio, count, duration, and forbidden items
If references matter, actually add assets in the creation input

steps.title: Save to My Prompts
steps.description: Open My Prompts, click Add Prompt, and fill in title, category, tags, body, and notes.
checklist: Titles should describe use case, not arbitrary numbers
Keep categories and tags consistent
Use notes for usage scenarios or replacement rules
List actions support copying and editing saved prompts

faqs.question: What is the difference between a prompt and a Skill?
faqs.answer: A prompt is the text you give the model. A Skill is an Agent execution capability. Choosing a Skill does not auto-fill fixed text into the input box.

faqs.question: Why is adding a prompt a modal instead of a permanent form?
faqs.answer: Add uses a modal so the list page stays focused on search and management. After save or cancel, you return to the original list position.

account.label: Account & purchases
account.title: Manage plans, points, and orders
account.summary: Open Profile from the avatar menu to view the current plan, points balance, profile, plan purchase, orders, usage history, points ledger, and account security.

flow.title: Choose a product
flow.detail: Open Plans in Profile and compare benefits

flow.title: Confirm the order
flow.detail: Choose quantity and payment method, then verify amount and points

flow.title: Complete payment
flow.detail: Continue on the secure checkout page by channel

flow.title: Verify benefits
flow.detail: Return to orders, plan, and points history to confirm the result

steps.title: Enter Profile from the avatar menu
steps.description: The top-right avatar menu keeps the Profile entry. The sidebar help entry no longer jumps to personal details again.
checklist: Overview: plan, balance, and recent records
Profile: display name and email
Security: change password
Orders and points sections: check every change

steps.title: Choose and purchase a plan
steps.description: In Plans, click upgrade or buy, compare price/points/benefits in the plan modal first, then enter the independent secure payment page.
checklist: Confirm plan name and benefits
Confirm purchase quantity
Confirm payment method and total amount
Benefits activate only after successful payment

steps.title: Check payment and points results
steps.description: After payment, return to Profile and check order status. Credited points, plan changes, usage deductions, and failed refunds appear in their own records.
checklist: Orders: pending, paid, canceled, or manual confirmation
Points history: balance increases and adjustments
Usage: generation tasks and model-call deductions
If results are delayed, refresh records first and do not pay the same order twice

faqs.question: Why is plan upgrade a modal, but payment is not?
faqs.answer: Plan comparison should stay fast, so it uses an in-workbench modal. When amount, quantity, and payment channel are involved, checkout moves to a dedicated secure page so the full order can be reviewed.

faqs.question: What if the order is paid but benefits have not changed yet?
faqs.answer: Refresh status in order history first. Some payment callbacks may lag slightly, and manual channels need order confirmation. Do not create multiple orders for the same need.

troubleshooting.label: FAQ
troubleshooting.title: Troubleshoot loading, generation, and display issues
troubleshooting.summary: When a page is blank, data loads slowly, models cannot be selected, or media will not open, first locate the broken stage and avoid resubmitting or double-charging.
outcomes: Tell page issues from task issues
Avoid creating generation or payment requests twice

flow.title: Confirm the page
flow.detail: Refresh the current page and check login state

flow.title: Locate the stage
flow.detail: Separate data loading, planning, submit, and generation failures

flow.title: Read the message
flow.detail: Adjust based on page errors and task status

flow.title: Retry safely
flow.detail: Only retry failed items, not successful requests

steps.title: Page data stays empty for a long time
steps.description: First check network and login state, then use in-page refresh or retry. Do not switch around and repeatedly click create while loading.
checklist: Look for an explicit error message
Reopen the current section
Use the matching retry button for assets, projects, or history failures
If still empty, confirm the current account really has data

steps.title: Models or Skills cannot be selected
steps.description: Lists only show currently executable capabilities. Skills are also filtered by workspace, so different pages may show different options.
checklist: Keep smart planning on to use default capabilities
Do not type model names manually when the list is empty
Skills that do not match the current workspace are hidden

steps.title: Images or videos cannot preview
steps.description: Prefer opening the media itself for preview, then try download. Historical media needs a valid server URL and current-user permission.
checklist: Confirm the task already succeeded
Confirm media is not still processing
Reopen history to refresh the access URL
Do not share expired temporary links as long-term asset URLs

steps.title: Retry after generation or payment failure
steps.description: Only retry clearly failed tasks or unpaid orders. Do not resubmit successful tasks or pay the same order again.
checklist: Record the error shown on the page
On generation failure, adjust parameters or references first
On payment failure, continue the original order instead of creating a new one
If balance looks wrong, check points history and usage records

faqs.question: Will refreshing the page lose projects?
faqs.answer: Creative sessions, Canvas, assets, drama, and generation records are saved on the server per signed-in user. Page refresh reloads them and does not rely on the browser to store large business data.

faqs.question: When should I create a task again?
faqs.answer: Only create a new one when the original task clearly failed, was canceled, or the request has changed. Resubmitting while a task is still running increases wait time and points risk.
